scoring_justification: Binding energies are recomputed from the agent's own formation energies using Eq.2; formation energies and migration barriers are compared against paper gold with tolerances (±0.5 eV and ±0.1 eV) and monotonicity checks; maximum occupancy is an exact-match discrete claim. This combines recompute, reference match, and structural checks, giving the overall strongest tier as recompute.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported formation energies (Table 1) and migration barriers (Section 4, Fig. 7) embedded as gold references for scoring.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Table 1 and text of the paper 'Cluster formation and eventual mobility of helium in a tungsten grain boundary' (DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2018.11.029): formation energies at the interface and V-interface columns; migration barriers of 0.35, 0.45, 0.54 eV for 1,2,3 He atoms from Section 4.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Exact transcription of the published numerical values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's actual results, used as hidden references to verify reproduction.

outputs.description: Formation energies of He clusters at the interface groove and inside the vacancy, to be compared against paper-reported reference values within tolerance and checked for monotonic increase with N_He.
Atom-by-atom binding energies derived from formation energies, compared against paper-reported reference values within tolerance and checked for the expected trend.

NEB migration barriers for 1, 2, and 3 He atoms moving along the most stable groove, compared against paper-reported reference values within tolerance and checked for monotonic increase with cluster size.
Maximum number of He atoms directly accommodated inside the interfacial monovacancy and whether spillover occurs for larger clusters. Exact values: 7 and true, as per the paper.

output_contract.notes: All scored quantities are derived from DFT calculations using open-source tools. The target policies are reference_match for energies (compared against hidden paper gold with tolerances) and exact_match for the discrete max_occupancy result. The checker will also enforce structural trends (monotonicity for formation energies and barriers).
